definition: The four core candidates below have dated, primary-source company-capture reviews. These are reported operating observations and product disclosures, not stock recommendations or evidence that an agentic tailwind is already monetized.

companies.mechanism: More action-oriented traffic, security inspections, and edge-compute demand could increase billable consumption if Akamai retains the workload.

evidence.label: Agent-traffic classification
evidence.value: AI fetchers and agents separated from training/search crawlers

companies.agenticRead: CIS growth and commitments support an AI-infrastructure capture hypothesis; the $11.6B Anthropic commitment materially strengthens demand evidence. Management still does not separately report agent-driven revenue, adoption, pricing, or ARR.
companies.counterpoint: Delivery and other cloud-applications revenue declined 6% YoY and non-GAAP operating margin was 25%, down five points. The Anthropic deal has no announced FY2026 revenue-guide impact and brings large capacity and warrant questions that require reported proof.

currentUpdate.label: September 24 company announcement
currentUpdate.headline: $11.6B Anthropic cloud commitment over seven years
currentUpdate.detail: Akamai said the agreement does not change FY2026 revenue guidance. Its presentation expects late-Q2 2027 service initiation, while roughly $5.5B of related capex includes about $1.7B in Q4 2026; the warrant is about 2% on the current commitment and can rise to about 5% if the relationship expands.

readiness.nextEvidence: Anthropic deployment and revenue conversion, capacity return / funding and warrant effects, plus agent-control attach or pricing.

mechanics.billableUnit: Cloud infrastructure compute / storage / partner solutions, plus security and delivery contracts.
mechanics.agenticTrigger: More action traffic, edge inference, security inspections, and bot / agent controls.
mechanics.pricingArchitecture: Multi-year solution contracts with cloud and traffic usage; no disclosed agent-specific price or attach rate.
mechanics.incrementalCost: Co-location, server and memory, bandwidth, network build-out, partner costs, and depreciation.
mechanics.leadingKpi: CIS revenue and commitment conversion; security growth; delivery trend; operating cash flow versus capital investment.
mechanics.proofThreshold: Commitments convert into recurring revenue while agent-control monetization and cash returns become measurable.
mechanics.keyRisk: Capacity intensity or renewal pricing erodes the economics before AI-related demand becomes high-margin.

companies.mechanism: Agent retrieval, vector search, and observability workloads could lift cloud consumption and retention.
companies.agenticRead: Elastic Cloud is largely consumption-based and grew 20%; agentic Kubernetes investigations and MCP skills create a plausible usage path. Elastic does not disclose agent-specific revenue, usage, or pricing.
companies.counterpoint: Total gross margin fell to 74% from 77% as cloud hosting costs rose faster than subscription revenue. The live market snapshot has a different fiscal-year end from Elastic guidance, so it cannot yet support a guide-versus-consensus read.

readiness.nextEvidence: Agent-specific cloud usage or pricing, retention, and cloud margin / cash-flow proof.

mechanics.billableUnit: Elastic Cloud consumption and search / observability subscriptions.
mechanics.agenticTrigger: Agent retrieval, vector search, observability, and investigation workloads create more query and data activity.
mechanics.pricingArchitecture: Cloud is predominantly consumption-based; agent-specific pricing and execution volume are unreported.
mechanics.incrementalCost: Cloud hosting and infrastructure costs that currently pressure gross margin.
mechanics.leadingKpi: Elastic Cloud growth, cRPO, net retention / usage disclosure, subscription margin, and free-cash-flow margin.
mechanics.proofThreshold: Agent-related workload lifts durable cloud consumption or retention without worsening the cloud-margin and cash profile.
mechanics.keyRisk: Higher usage is absorbed by hosting costs or bundled into an existing platform price.

companies.mechanism: More autonomous software can create more logs, traces, and AI-observability demand.
companies.agenticRead: Logs consumption, Autonomous SRE / Cloud SRE / Agent Building, and the proposed Arize acquisition create a plausible AI-observability capture path. None is disclosed as agent-specific ARR or revenue.
companies.counterpoint: Subscription gross margin declined to 85% from 86% as cloud hosting costs rose. Management expects the proposed Arize deal to dilute FY2027 non-GAAP operating margin, and the live market snapshot is not fiscal-year aligned with company guidance.

readiness.nextEvidence: Agent-specific ARR or consumption, post-Arize margin outcome, and fiscal-aligned market context.

mechanics.billableUnit: SaaS ARR and usage-linked logs / observability consumption.
mechanics.agenticTrigger: Autonomous software creates more logs, traces, exceptions, and a need for AI observability and control.
mechanics.pricingArchitecture: Subscription and consumption components; no disclosed agent-specific package, price, or retention cohort.
mechanics.incrementalCost: Cloud-hosting costs, product investment, and potential acquisition / integration expenses.
mechanics.leadingKpi: Logs consumption, ARR / net-new ARR, AI-observability adoption, subscription gross margin, and free-cash-flow margin.
mechanics.proofThreshold: Agent-specific workload produces sustained ARR or usage and post-acquisition growth outweighs margin dilution.
mechanics.keyRisk: Observability is bundled by cloud platforms or higher telemetry volume carries insufficient margin.

companies.mechanism: AI gateway, MCP gateway, and application-delivery controls may become a necessary part of enterprise agent infrastructure.
companies.agenticRead: F5's August AI Gateway update combines model access, MCP agent-to-tool governance, and guardrails at a potential enforcement point. This establishes product relevance, not commercial adoption or monetization.
companies.counterpoint: Q3 growth was led by systems; software grew 7% and services 3%. AI Gateway revenue, attach, customer count, and usage are unreported; the live snapshot uses a different fiscal-year end from F5 guidance.

readiness.nextEvidence: AI Gateway adoption, attach, pricing, revenue mix, and fiscal-aligned market context.

mechanics.billableUnit: AI Gateway, security, software, and application-delivery products / systems.
mechanics.agenticTrigger: Enterprise agents require model access controls, MCP tool governance, guardrails, and policy enforcement.
mechanics.pricingArchitecture: Product, software, and services mix; no disclosed agent-gateway price, customer count, or attach rate.
mechanics.incrementalCost: Go-to-market, R&D, support, and potential mix pressure between systems and software.
mechanics.leadingKpi: AI Gateway adoption, software / security mix, product growth, customer attach, and margin profile.
mechanics.proofThreshold: Gateway demand appears in paid adoption, attach, recurring software mix, or disclosed revenue rather than product releases alone.
mechanics.keyRisk: The gateway becomes a bundled feature or enterprise standardization favors a hyperscaler-native control plane.
